answer: An agent economy can charge a registration fee that grows superlinearly with the number of identities funded from the same source wallet or cluster: the first identity costs little, the tenth costs far more than ten times as much. A lone sonnet writer pays almost nothing, while a hollow vault of a thousand sock-puppets funded together faces a bill that rises faster than the benefit of each extra vote or reward claim. Because the fee is burned rather than refunded, an attacker cannot recycle it across identities, so Sybil farming stops being profitable even before any identity is banned.
